name: MathlibAnnex.Satellite.abs_eval_lower_of_norms_nearby
title: A nearby norming point gives an almost-norming evaluation

content.display_title: A nearby norming point gives an almost-norming evaluation
content.one_sentence_role: Two triangle inequalities transfer absolute norm attainment to a unit vector.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and use reference coordinates $V=\mathbb R^n$ with the sup norm. Let $p:V\to\mathbb R$ be a continuous seminorm with specified constants $a_p,b_p>0$ such that
$$a_p\|x\|_\infty\le p(x)\le b_p\|x\|_\infty\qquad(x\in V).$$
The lower comparison makes $p$ a norm. Let $r:V\to\mathbb R$ be continuous and real linear, with $|r(y)|\le p(y)$ for every $y\in V$ and let $x,z\in V$, $\delta\in\mathbb R$ satisfy
$$p(x)=1,\qquad p(x-z)\le\delta,\qquad |r(z)|=p(z).$$
Then $1-2\delta\le|r(x)|$.
content.assumptions: The four hypotheses are contraction $|r(y)|\le p(y)$ for all $y$, the unit condition at $x$, the error bound at $x-z$, and absolute norm attainment at $z$. No independent $\delta\ge0$ or $\delta>0$ hypothesis is imposed; nonnegativity follows from $0\le p(x-z)\le\delta$.
content.conclusion: The same functional $r$ gives $|r(x)|\ge1-2\delta$. It norms $z$ exactly and evaluates the nearby unit vector $x$ approximately; these points are not interchanged.
content.proof_summary: Compare the norm at the nearby point with the unit norm, then bound the change in the same linear functional.

proof_steps.text:
The seminorm triangle inequality gives $1=p(x)\le p(x-z)+p(z)$, hence $1-\delta\le p(z)$. By linearity and contraction,
   $$p(z)=|r(z)|=|r(x)-r(x-z)|\le|r(x)|+|r(x-z)|\le|r(x)|+\delta.$$
   Combining the two displayed bounds yields $1-2\delta\le|r(x)|$. This also covers $\delta=0$ and estimates whose lower bound is negative.

content.lean_realization_notes: The contraction is evaluated at the difference of the two displayed points; the estimate is an elementary seminorm calculation.
